newsitem.title: USA: Asarco reports 14 percent rise in earnings.
newsitem.headline: Asarco reports 14 percent rise in earnings.

text.p: Asarco Inc. Thursday reported a 14 percent rise in first quarter profits and said lower production costs offset the impact of a drop in copper prices.
The giant mining company said it earned $40.6 million or 95 cents a share vs. year-earlier profits of $35.7 million or 84 cents a share.
Sales, however, fell to $715.6 million from $735 million.
Asarco said the average prices for copper in the first quarter was $1.11 a pound, down from $1.18 a year earlier.
"Asarco's earnings improved in the first quarter of 1997 despite lower copper prices," said Chairman Richard de J. Osborne.

"The increase in net earnings in the first quarter of 1997 is principally the result of lower costs at the company's domestic copper operations, gains recorded from our price protection programme, reduced interest expense and a reduction in the company's effective tax rate," he said.

The Asarco chairman said "the fundamentals of the metal markets, particularly in the case of copper are quite good," noting that inventories of copper are at historically low levels and demand continues to be strong.
Asarco's stock was unchanged at $28.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon.
